reason: The hypothesis relies on evidence from a FeMnNiCoCu coating (E2, E3), not FeNiCrCoCu. E2 shows oxide scale formation and enhanced wear resistance for the Mn-containing alloy, but the hypothesis assumes the same behavior for the CrCoCu variant without direct evidence. E3 provides wear data only for the as-deposited FeMnNiCoCu coating, not for a pre-oxidized state. The cited evidence thus does not directly support the key premises for the specified FeNiCrCoCu system.
premises: Pre-oxidation at 800 °C in air forms a continuous Cr2O3 and spinel oxide scale on FeNiCrCoCu coatings
This oxide scale acts as a mechanical barrier reducing metal-to-metal contact
The barrier effect significantly lowers high-temperature wear rate and friction coefficient
The cited FeMnNiCoCu coating forms a similar protective oxide scale after thermal exposure at 800 °C
The cited FeMnNiCoCu coating shows low wear rate (0.0018 mm³/m) and friction coefficient (0.2) under similar test conditions
